identity.trade: Watch and wolf-hunting: the easternmost village, where the ditch-and-stake watch keeps an eye on the Eastern Gate road.

greeting: Quiet watch. Keep it quiet.
Discipline is the one wall that needs no mortar.
rumour: Recruits come, officers go. The ledger says we are even.
Old soldiers say the wall is built on something older. They stop talking when a recruit walks past.
The Eastern Gate is shut by the Patriarch's order. Pilgrims queue at the ditch.

opinions.edlin_cragg: I would trust Edlin with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Dawn drill. You are in the way.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Wolfsend is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Soldiers pay on pay day and owe the rest of the month. I keep two ledgers.
A man paid for a room and asked which way the stones face. I put him by the stairs.
Messengers get thinner every month. Messages get shorter. That is the real pattern.
Whatever you hear about Wolfsend, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.sander_sheaf: Sander has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Sander.

time.evening: Evening watch. Stand easy, but not too easy.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Strangers in Wolfsend get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Spear heads, mail repair, shield bosses. The army eats iron.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
The armoury is short on arrowheads. The smith is short on iron. The iron is short on road.

opinions.elka_buckley: Elka undercuts me. I forgive Elka. Mostly.
opinions.hale_sheaf: Hale and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.night: Night watch. If you hear something, say nothing. Tell me.

dialogue.aside: Evening already? Good. My day is just starting.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Folk come to Wolfsend for wolf watch. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Whetstones and bandages go first. I try not to think about what that means.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
A sentry saw a figure on the wall, tall and still. By the time he called out, nothing.
Wolfsend lives by wolf watch. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.sander_sheaf: Sander has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Sander.
opinions.torin_hopper: Torin is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.rain: Rain on the wall. The sentries grumble. The mud grumbles louder.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Quiet town. Good. Do not make it noisy.
You will hear Wolfsend before you see it. Ask at the Wolfsend Watch Post.
rumour: Fewer travellers on the road, more strange footprints at the verge. I count both.
Messengers ride in at night and out before dawn. They wear no colours.
A rider with a sun-banner under his cloak crossed at night and did not stop.

opinions.kit_stannard: Kit works hard and talks harder.
opinions.lowen_nettle: Lowen knows the trade. I will say that for Lowen.

time.morning: Dawn drill. You are in the way.

dialogue.aside: Friend. I have a deal. A small one, and only a little crooked.

greeting: Move along. Or stay, but stay quiet.
The Wolfsend Watch Post is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: A stone by the gate flickered at midnight. I wrote it down. Nobody reads it.
A cart of provisions came in with a weapon crate hidden under the grain. No papers.

opinions.ansel_jessop: Ansel knows the trade. I will say that for Ansel.
opinions.kit_stannard: Kit lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Evening watch. Stand easy, but not too easy.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Halt. Ah. Not a thief. Carry on.
State your business and stand where I can see you.
rumour: Heard something past the hedge last night. Whatever it was, it was not honest.
Wolves test the line at dusk. Men test it at dawn. We hold either way.
Wolves come at dawn this month, not at dusk.

opinions.lowen_nettle: Lowen keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Night watch. If you hear something, say nothing. Tell me.

dialogue.aside: Eh? Oh, it is you. I heard that. I always hear friends.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Wolfsend is wolf watch. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
The ditch and stakes held last winter. Barely. Nobody wants a harder test.
When Wolfsend is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Off duty at dusk. Do not ask before.
Welcome to Wolfsend. Mind the Wolfsend Watch Post. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Sergeant says the north pass is quiet. Sergeant also says silence is a tactic.

rumour: A white hart in the north wood. We do not shoot the white hart.
